messages.subject: adding polygon to density surface
parts:
Hi all,

I have been making a plot which is a density surface and overlaying a transparency that represents error in the surface.  The higher the error the more transparent the plot.  I have done what I thought would be the hard part and made the plot but now I am having trouble adding a polygon to it.  The toy example below is a pretty course representation of what i have done but should give you an idea.  The polygons I have for the plots are coastlines and I may have several polygons per plot. 

I also have two other questions detailed in the code below.  These are on switching the direction of the transparency scale and  changing the plot colour. 

Any help would be much appreciated.

Many Thanks
Lindesay Scott-Hayward



# Toy example for ggplot
x = 1:20
y = 1:20

grid = expand.grid(x, y)

# function values
func = (grid[,1]^2)/1000

# error values to be added to the plot so that areas of high error are more transparent
knot = c(10,10)
errors = exp(-(sqrt(apply((grid-knot)^2, 1, sum))/1))

d = sqrt(apply((grid-knot)^2, 1, sum))
circ.err  = - d^2 * log (d)/100
circ.err[190] = 0
p = ggplot(grid, aes(grid[,1], grid[,2], fill = func, alpha = errors)) + geom_tile()
p
# the addition of transparency to represent errors works fine but I wonder is it possible to change the scale around so that 0 error is represented full colour (zero transparency) and maximum error represents maximum transparency (i.e. little colour showing on plot)

# polygon adding
pol = data.frame(x1 = c(12, 16, 16, 12), x2 = c(12, 12, 16, 16))
p + layer(geom = 'polygon', data=p1)

# this gives an error of differing lengths

# Lastly how do i change the colour of my plot.  I have tried
p = ggplot(grid, aes(grid[,1], grid[,2], fill = func, alpha = errors)) + geom_tile() + scale_colour_gradientn(colours = terrain.colors(100))
p
 # but it does not change the colour of my plot

messages.subject: RE: adding polygon to density surface
parts:
Hi,

 

The trick is the following;

 

p = ggplot(grid, aes(grid[,1], grid[,2], fill = func, alpha = circ.err)) + geom_tile() +

scale_fill_gradientn(colours = topo.colors(100)) +
scale_alpha_continuous(to = c(0,1), trans = "reverse") +

theme_bw()

 

is the same as:

p = ggplot(data = grid, aes(x = grid[,1], y = grid[,2], fill = func, alpha = circ.err)) + geom_tile(aes(x = grid[,1], y = grid[,2], fill = func, alpha = circ.err)) …

 

so to simplify tha syntax, it assumes shared aesthetics are the same between geoms if the contrary is not specified.

 

In the case of the polygons you want to draw;

# polygon adding

pol = data.frame(Var1 = c(12, 16, 16, 12), Var2 = c(12, 12, 16, 16))

p + layer(geom = 'polygon', data=pol) == p + layer(geom = 'polygon', data=pol, aes(x = grid[,1], y = grid[,2], fill = func, alpha = circ.err)))

 

the strange thing is that you don’t receive an error … (that’s why I forwarded the email also to the ggplot2 list) .. even this syntax produces the same result:

p + layer(geom = 'polygon', data=pol, mapping = aes(x = grid[,1], y = grid[,2]))

 

in any case, it seems you need to overcome the default aesthetics to

p + layer (data = pol, geom = "polygon", mapping = aes(x = Var1, y = Var2), alpha = I(1), fill = I("grey20"))

p + geom_polygon(data = pol, aes(x = Var1, y = Var2), alpha = I(1), fill = I("pink"))

 

(by the way, I think this is the first or second time I use ‘layer’ to make a plot)

 

Hope this helps, all the best,

fernadno
